To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Deregulation of apoptotic pathways is a hallmark of acute myeloid leukaemia and a key target for novel anti-leukaemic therapy.

apoptosis is dysregulated in leukemic cells, that these dysregulations play an important role in leukemia development and that the identification of the molecular defects in apoptotic pathways may lead to the development of novel therapies for leukemia.

(1) leukemic cells have abnormalities in the apoptotis pathway that are associated with resistance to chemotherapy; (2) these abnormalities are due to the overexpression of anti-apoptotic proteins and/or to the downregulation of pro-apoptotic proteins; (3) the identification of these abnormalities may be of help in the development of new therapies that target anti-apoptotic pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the apoptotic response in leukemic cells with the aim of understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in the deregulation of apoptosis and their role in leukemogenesis and chemoresistance.
understanding how apoptosis is deregulated in leukemic cells and how this deregulation contributes to the pathogenesis of the disease and to the development of drug-resistance.
the identification and characterization of the molecular mechanisms that determine the survival advantage of leukemic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
deregulation of apoptosis is a central event in the development of acute leukemia, contributing to the survival advantage and drug resistance of leukemic cells.

the dysregulation of the apoptosis in leukemic cells is an important mechanism of leukemic survival and drug resistance and that the study of the molecular pathways involved in the apoptotic dysregulation may lead to the identification and development of new therapeutic approaches.

the study of the apoptotic response of leukemic cells has contributed to the identification of potential targets for the development and testing of new drugs and to the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in the development of chemotherapeutic resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
apoptosis is an important target for new therapies of acute myeloid leukemias.

the deregulation of apoptosis plays a crucial role in the survival advantage of leukemic cells over normal hematopoietetic cells, in the development of resistance to chemotherapy treatment and in the development of leukemic relapses.

deregulation of apoptosis is a key event in leukemic cell survival and drug resistance and the identification of new drugs that target the apoptotic pathways in leukemic cells may represent an important therapeutic strategy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of the apoptotic response of leukemic cells has lead to the identification and characterization of new molecular pathways involved in the control of apoptosis.
apoptosis plays an essential role in the development and progression of acute myeloid leukaemia.
the apoptotic response is deregulated in acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) cells.
